content: Reserpine is prescribed to treat high blood pressure. It achieves this by reducing your heart rate and relaxing the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily throughout your body. Additionally, it is used to manage severe agitation in patients with mental disorders. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Reserpine is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Reserpine helps control high blood pressure or symptoms of agitation but does not cure these conditions. Continue taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, as abruptly discontinuing the medication may lead to increased blood pressure and unwanted side effects. Before taking reserpine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to reserpine, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and medications), or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially amitriptyline (Elavil), clomipramine (Anafranil), desipramine (Norpramin), digoxin (Lanoxin), doxepin (Adapin, Sinequan), ephedrine, epinephrine, imipramine (Tofranil), MAO inhibitors, methylphenidate (Ritalin), nortriptyline (Aventyl, Pamelor), phenylephrine, protriptyline (Vivactil), quinidine (Quinaglute), trimipramine (Surmontil), and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease, gallstones, ulcers, ulcerative colitis, a history of depression, or if you have undergone electric shock therapy. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking reserpine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking reserpine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can exacerbate the side effects of reserpine. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet. Follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of reserpine, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for the missed one. Reserpine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: dizziness, loss of appetite, diarrhea, upset stomach, vomiting, stuffy nose, headache, dry mouth, or decreased sexual ability. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: depression, nightmares, fainting, slow heartbeat, chest pain, or swelling of the ankles or feet. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store reserpine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be monitored regularly to assess your response to reserpine. Your doctor may instruct you to check your pulse (heart rate) daily and will provide guidance on the expected rate. Ask your doctor or pharmacist to teach you how to measure your pulse. If your pulse is slower than it should be, contact your doctor before taking reserpine that day. Weigh yourself daily and notify your doctor if you experience rapid weight gain. Do not share your medication with anyone else. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
